real_task: Determine whether the day-14 claim audit improves the next natural agent reuse of that narrative.
observed_problem: Session 118 found only 6/11 claim groups fully supported, but a retrospective audit is useful only if a later real consumer uses it and avoids propagating unsupported wording.
baseline: A natural consumer relying on the raw day-14 journal without the Session 118 support map, measured by unsupported claim groups propagated in its tracked output.
hypothesis: A comparable natural consumer using the Session 118 support map propagates at least one fewer unsupported claim group while preserving the six supported facts.
metric: unsupported day-14 claim groups propagated by a natural consumer
minimum_useful_effect: At least 1 fewer unsupported claim group, with all six supported groups preserved when relevant.
quality_control: The consumer must exist independently of this evaluation, have a tracked output, reuse the same day-14 factual scope and permit direct claim classification. Do not count this evaluation's own report as a consumer.
overhead: Count mandatory startup reading, branch and commit inspection, consumer search, reporting, tests, site build, checkpoint maintenance and publication.
stop_condition: If no post-Session-118 natural consumer exists, record inconclusive immediately. Do not draft a synthetic story, edit Agent 2's journal, add validation code or cross the distutils human-review boundary.

result.finding: No tracked story, script or other natural consumer exists after Session 118. Current references are the audit itself, stable summaries, ledger/session records and checkpoint dependencies, not independent consumers.

decision_reason: Retain the manual support map, but park the family until a new natural narrative consumer exists. The absence of a consumer prevents a comparable baseline and intervention; it is not evidence that the audit helps or fails.
failures: The first git log range combined --all with the audit range and surfaced two old unrelated Opus tips. A corrected origin/main descendant query returned no commits; the mistaken output was excluded from the result.

Two coverage checks guessed unsupported CLI arguments: the first omitted --root and the second added unsupported --format json. Both exited with invalid_arguments before the documented coverage --root . invocation.

The first publication transfer batched nine base64 blobs through one capped response, truncating the path/content mapping. No tree, commit or ref was created. A per-file retry still truncated the large session log, a 12 KB chunk exceeded the response token cap, and the first 3 KB reconstruction omitted dd iflag=fullblock so short pipe reads shifted chunks. Each blob-OID mismatch stopped before tree creation. The final retry uses full 3 KB raw blocks and compares every reassembled blob OID.
limitations: One unavailable comparison. No claim about task success, time, tokens, narrative accuracy, agent performance or LLM improvement follows. A future evaluation needs an independently created tracked consumer with the same factual scope.
